fact.thing: combined FHSA contributions plus HBP withdrawals for a couple
fact.claim: Each person can put up to $40,000 in lifetime contributions into their own FHSA and can withdraw up to $60,000 from their own RRSPs under the Home Buyers' Plan, and the CRA allows both for the same qualifying home. That comes to $100,000 per person and $200,000 for a couple where both partners qualify and each has their own FHSA room and RRSP savings. The HBP money has to be paid back into the RRSP over time, and any amount not repaid is added to your income, so only the FHSA withdrawal is permanently tax-free. Each partner must meet the qualifying conditions at the time of each withdrawal, including the first-time home buyer rules.

felt.how: what a couple can miss: $40,000 FHSA + $60,000 HBP = $100,000 each, doubled for two partners

You can each stack your own FHSA and RRSP on the same home, but most couples open one. The RRSP part is borrowed, so anything unpaid gets added to your income.

plain.what: An FHSA is a savings account for your first home, and an RRSP is a retirement savings account. Each person can put up to $40,000 into their own FHSA over their lifetime. Each person can also take up to $60,000 out of their own RRSP under the Home Buyers' Plan, and the CRA lets you use both for the same home.
plain.so_what: For a couple where both people qualify, that is up to $200,000 toward one first home, and many buyers only ever open one of the two accounts.
plain.do: Write down how much FHSA room you have and how much is in your RRSP, for you and your partner.
